seed_stability_checked.why_it_matters: the one route by which a pure transport change could reach the science: if an abandoned call were retried under a different seed, then shortening the timeout would raise the retry count and thereby change what was sampled.

disclosed_weaknesses: the 120s value is calibrated on one day of provider behaviour (58 successful calls). On 2026-07-29 the same endpoint produced successful calls as long as 1005s TOTAL. That is not by itself evidence against 120s: the pinned models stream, so an httpx read timeout bounds the gap between consecutive chunks, not a call's total duration, and a long generation whose chunks keep arriving never trips it. What would trip it is any single inter-chunk gap above 120s. The ledger records only the start and end of each call, so inter-chunk gaps cannot be reconstructed from it after the fact, and the true margin under that earlier regime is therefore unmeasured rather than measured-and-adequate.

shortening the timeout converts some calls that would eventually have returned into abandoned unknown_charge reservations. Those are permanently counted against the uncertain-spend ceiling and can never be reconciled to a definite outcome.

the amendment is calibrated on gemma-4-31B, which is the only model failing. It applies to every model because http_timeout is a client-wide pin, so the other three models get a shorter timeout they have not needed.

evidence_2026_08_01.cost: measured progress over the amendment-6 window was 4 cells in 3.3 hours, which extrapolates to roughly 12 days for the 362 remaining cells.
evidence_2026_08_01.failure_shape: every failure is 'Request timed out.' at the 600s httpx read timeout; every success completed in under 47s. The distribution is bimodal with nothing in between.
evidence_2026_08_01.headroom: 120s is about 2.6x the slowest successful call observed on this date, and time-to-first-chunk is strictly less than total call duration.
evidence_2026_08_01.no_first_chunk: google/gemma-4-31B-it is streaming-pinned, so the httpx read timeout bounds the wait for the NEXT chunk. A timeout therefore means 600 seconds elapsed without a single chunk arriving: the request produced nothing, rather than being slow.
evidence_2026_08_01.not_a_size_effect: successes and failures have indistinguishable prompt sizes (median estimated tokens 10972 vs 10964, identical 30649 max)
